pr_title: DCS work nicely with collectible AssemblyLoadContext
pr_body:
This replaces the draft PR (#88791) that I was using earlier. The pre-requisite changes that were staged in the first few commits of that draft got checked in under their own PR with proper contributor attribution (#73893), so this PR cherry-picks the rest of that draft and then addresses the feedback.

Fixes #77877
pr_comments: The only change that needs to happen is move the second check inside of the locks then this is good to merge.

issue_context.title: DataContractSerializer caches collectible types in statics

review_comments: It's only a style thing, but did you consider having providing an indexer property instead of switching to Get and Set methods?

Sort of an evolution of the context-aware side of the design that got away from the original usage pattern. An indexer would fit the original code. But the nullable notation of the original code was incorrect, even if our code was dilligent about null-checking. Maybe I've still got Monday brain, but I don't know of a way to make the getter nullable and the setter non-nullable... notation-wise anyway.
Is this safe to do outside of a lock?
I found [the documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.conditionalweaktable-2?view=net-7.0#thread-safety) that says it is thread safe.

The docs say it is - [ConditionalWeakTable - Thread Safety](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.conditionalweaktable-2?view=net-7.0#thread-safety)

I looked at the code for CWT quickly and see it's using an object hash to index into fixed size arrays of entries which appear to be a self-rolled linked-list. I didn't dig into all the accessing and writing of these linked lists.

This is the slow branch of the code. I can move this inside the lock if we feel better about that.

So, TryGetValue may be safe outside the lock here... but the GetValue() method following here executes the `createValueCallback` outside of it's lock which presents the same race that we have with ConcurrentDictionary. I'll update this.
FWIW, the 4.8 source for CWT also makes strong claims about thread safety. https://referencesource.microsoft.com/#mscorlib/system/runtime/compilerservices/ConditionalWeakTable.cs,41
The TryGetValue should be inside the lock to avoid race conditions (which would be non-critical, but still something you want to avoid). Same for the collectibleTable.

Why would TryGetValue need to be inside the lock? This is a ConcurrentDictionary, so TryGetValue should be ok outside of the lock. If two threads pass this check and find nothing, the lock still gates them and the 'GetOrAdd' will have the first one do the work, and the second one just does a simple 'Get.' Am I missing something about TryGetValue that makes it unsafe outside of the lock?

Wait. Nevermind. I retract my absent-minded statement. The whole point of adding a lock was to have the check inside it since GetOrAdd runs the add delegate in both cases regardless. And somehow I forgot that important point when recreating this PR. :/
